CATHETER ABLATION OF FIBRILLATION 
Hangsik Shin l , Yonghyeon Yun l , Eun Bo Shim 2 , Hui-Nam Pak l 
Division of Cardioloty, Yonsei University Health System, Korea J, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering,

BaCkground: Although radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) is effective in rhythm control for 
fibrillation, remaining gap is a main reason for recurrence in clinical setting. Therefore, we 
investigated the effects of ablation gaps on wave dynamics by utilizing in-silico modeling. 
Methods: We generated continuous fibrillation s) in 2D bi-domain human cardiac model and 
analyzed the last 3 seconds data to quantify spatiotemporal organization of fibrillation. Linear 
ablation lesions were generated by 2.5 mm sized dots without conduction and 0.25 mm 
peri-ablation low conductivity at 80% critical mass region . We compared spatiotemporal 
distributions of wavebreak points (WB), phase singularity points CPS), dominant frequency (OF), 
and fibrillation cycle lengths (CL) depending on the size of critical mass (l00 %, 90%, 80%, and 
70%) and number of gaps (G 1, G2, and G3). 
Results: I. As reducing critical mass from 100% to 90% and 80 %, WB (9.02±4.74, .6.59±4.11, 2.09 
±2.24, p<O.OOl), PS (25.78±8.55 , 20.02±9.26, 6.60±5.23, p<O.OOl), and OF (3.98±0.54 , 3.84±0.61, 
2.46±0.81 Hz, p<O.OOl) were decreased, and fibrillation CLs were increased (204.92±86.38, 220.08 
±90.l2, 250.12±111.55 ms, p<O.OOl). At critical mass 70%, fi brillation was finally terminated. 2. 
When we compared G 1, G2, and G3, exiting wavelet formed regu lar tachycardia in G 1, but became 
disorganized in G2 and G3 by wave-wave interactions. 3. The WB (3.72±2.78 , 8.57±5.02, 2.09± 
2.23 , 5.56±3.22 , p<O.OOl), PS (l2.24±7.03 , 26 .67±10.85, 6.60±5.23, 17.13±6.14 , p<O.OOl ), and 
fibrillation CL (262.88±128.05 , 203.59±81.48, 250.12±11 1.55 , 212.83±92 .50 ms, p<O.OO 1) were 
different in exit region of GO, G 1,02, and 03 respectively . 
Conclusion(s): Wave-dynamics and the degree of organiza tio n of fibri llation chan ged depending 
on the number of gaps and critical mass size. Virtual ablation sche me in 20 bi-domain cardiac 
model can be utilized for defining the mechanism of effecti ve or fai led arrhythmia control after 
catheter ablation.
